text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
NeedsMoney(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for college tuition.
OrdersTakeout(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHall(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendsTimeEating(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
AtSchool(x) ::: x is at Mary's school.
Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → NeedsMoney(x)) ::: If people at Mary's school work in student jobs, then they need to earn money.
∀x (OrdersTakeout(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people order takeout frequently, then they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrdersTakeout(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHall(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People order takeout frequently or enjoy the dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHall(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people enjoy the dining hall meals and recipes, then they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHall(x) → SpendsTimeEating(x)) ::: If people enjoy the dining hall meals, then they spend a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends.
Hannah :: at Mary's school.
Hannah :: works in student jobs.
Hannah :: needs to earn money to help pay for her college tuition if she works in student jobs.
Conclusion:
AtSchool(Hannah) ∧ (¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∨ (PickyEater(Hannah) → SpendsTimeEating(Hannah))) ::: Hannah is at Mary's school and she either is not a picky eater or, if she is, then she spends a lot of her time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
